defect.proposed_fix: Replace the citation metadata with 564 U.S. 229 (2011); parallel_cite 131 S. Ct. 2419; 180 L. Ed. 2d 285; neutral_cite 2011 U.S. LEXIS 4560; retain U.S. Supreme Court and 2011.

reasons: Lake citations.display is 564 U.S. 229, not 565 U.S. 1100.
Content frontmatter also gives 564 U.S. 229 (2011), 131 S. Ct. 2419, 180 L. Ed. 2d 285, and 2011 U.S. LEXIS 4560.
The asserted 565 U.S. 1100 / 2011 U.S. LEXIS 8943 citation package is not confirmed by the disclosed Davis lake record.
Content frontmatter lists home [[The Good-Faith Exception]] with role Key — Progeny (good faith).
The lake scope note states that Davis extends the Leon good-faith line to objectively reasonable reliance on binding appellate precedent later overruled.
The opinion text repeatedly frames the decision as applying the good-faith exception to blameless reliance on binding appellate precedent.
residual_risks: The body Appears on section lists The Exclusionary Rule rather than The Good-Faith Exception, but the frontmatter home assertion under review is supported.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Align the visible Appears on section with the frontmatter home if both are intended to describe the same placement.

reasons: The opinion states the question is whether to apply exclusion when police search in compliance with binding precedent later overruled, then holds such searches are not subject to the exclusionary rule.
The text says the search followed Eleventh Circuit Gonzalez precedent to the letter and that all agree the officers acted in strict compliance with then-binding Circuit law and were not culpable.
The conclusion repeats that when police conduct a search in objectively reasonable reliance on binding appellate precedent, the exclusionary rule does not apply.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep the rule limited to objectively reasonable reliance on binding appellate precedent; the disclosed authority does not support a broader rule for nonbinding precedent.
